newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends lower, tech stocks surge in mixed session.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends lower, tech stocks surge in mixed session.

text.p: Stocks finished broadly mixed on Tuesday, as blue chips registered small losses while technology stocks extended their recent scorching gains.
The Dow Jones industrial average fell 10.91 points to close at 8,187.54.
Broader indexes were generally higher, however, and the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite index posted its third consecutive record high. The Nasdaq rose 16.08 points, or 1 percent, to 1,621.53.
In the broader market, advancing issues beat decliners 1,595 to 1,236, on volume of 526 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The session highlighted a recent trend in which increasingly impatient investors move between various stock groups at the first sign of a shift in market psychology.

"This market has been marked by group and sector rotations in very short time frames," Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "With the primary market languishing, Nasdaq and the techs are pressing higher."

A main reason blue chips have hit a wall is a run-up in interest rates after recent evidence suggesting economic growth may be accelerating. Rates edged higher for the third straight session today, weighing on the performance of financial stocks.
The yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond climbed to 6.49 percent from 6.48 percent on Monday.
"One disappointing area today was financial services, which continues to trade in lock-step with the yield curve," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
Among banks, Chase Manhattan Corp. fell 1-7/16 to 109-9/16 and BankAmerica Corp. shed 1-5/8 to 71-7/8.

The Dow's tepid performance aside, the day belonged to technology stocks. Intel Corp. rose 2-15/16 to 99-11/16 after briefly brushing past the 100-point mark, while Microsoft Corp. rose 1-3/4 to 143-5/16 and disk drive maker Western Digital Corp. added 5-3/8 to 45-1/2.
"The chip stocks were on fire, the software names were on fire and the disk drive makers were on fire," Orlando said.
Networking leader Cisco Systems Inc. rose 5/16 to 81-15/16 ahead of the release of its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings.

After the close, Cisco reported its operating profit rose 34 percent, matching official Wall Street expectations. Even so, Cisco fell to 79-3/4 in after-hours trading, suggesting Wall Street's unofficial expectations may have been higher still.

Among individual issues, Aetna Inc. tumbled 14-1/4 to 102-3/4 after the company reported weaker-than-expected second-quarter results. Smith Barney downgraded the shares, citing disappointment with Aetna's managed care results.
Lone Star Steakhouse & Saloon Inc. fell 4 points to 18 after warning its third-quarter results would fail to meet Wall Street estimates.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 2.07 points to 952.37.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues, also known as the Wilshire 5,000 -- rose 35.481, or 0.39 percent, to a new high of 9,040.545.
